citation.title: Accelerating metamaterial topology optimization using deep super-resolution networks
citation.authors: Ajendra Singh, Shubham Saurabh, Abhinav Gupta, Rajib Chowdhury

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The trained EDSR predicts 192 × 192 metamaterial layouts from 48 × 48 SIMP layouts at 5–7% of the conventional same-resolution computational cost.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Abstract states 5–7% of conventional cost (about 14.3–20× speed-up). Table 1 gives a concrete case: 457 sec / 24 sec = 19.04×, including low-resolution generation and prediction (Section 4.1).
claim.alternatives: Abstract and conclusion also claim accurate reconstruction; the conclusion reports volume-fraction error below 2%, pixel error within 3%, objective-function error about 3%, and IoU above 0.90.

baseline.implementation: 55-line Python/FEniCS topology-optimization code cited for data generation (Section 4); comparator implementation details not further stated
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel Xeon 6230 CPU and NVIDIA Quadro P2200 GPU system; method-specific allocation not stated (Section 4)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Xeon 6230 CPU and NVIDIA Quadro P2200 GPU (Section 4)
baseline.problem_size: 48 × 48 low-resolution input to 192 × 192 high-resolution prediction; comparison at 192 × 192 (Abstract; Section 4)
baseline.classical_time: 457 sec (bulk modulus, Table 1); other objective averages: 493 sec (shear modulus, Table 3), 365 sec (elastic modulus, Table 5), 386 sec (Poisson ratio, Table 7)
baseline.ml_time: 24 sec (bulk modulus, Table 1); other objective averages: 26 sec (shear modulus, Table 3), 26 sec (elastic modulus, Table 5), 24 sec (Poisson ratio, Table 7); includes low-resolution generation and prediction (Section 4.1)
baseline.training_time: not stated; described as a one-time offline expenditure (Section 3)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; dataset generation described in Section 3.1
baseline.quality_metric: Volume-fraction error, objective-function error, pixel MSE, and IoU (Sections 3.4 and 4; Tables 2, 4, 6, 8)
baseline.quality_gap: Average errors are reported against high-resolution reference topologies, e.g. bulk-modulus case: 1.95% volume fraction, 3.03% objective function, 2.24% pixel MSE, IoU 0.92 (Table 2); not a matched-quality comparison to a converged classical run.

R1.evidence: Sections 3.4 and 4: prediction quality is assessed against high-resolution references, but the time comparison does not establish equal design quality or equal optimization budget; classical stopping details are unstated.

R2.evidence: Section 4: both approaches are reported on the same CPU/GPU system; no inefficient solver, abstract-baseline discrepancy, or excess iterations are established.

R3.evidence: Section 3 describes offline training and dataset preparation, but no training or data-generation costs are quantified and no break-even is given.

R4.evidence: Section 3.4: predicted topologies are meshed and objective functions recomputed; volume error is reported, but infeasible or failed designs are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: 150 held-out test samples per objective; four objectives are evaluated (Section 4).

notes: The paper says held-out test samples are used but does not report an out-of-distribution test.
